edges.reason: Caller-controlled msg.sender indexes and mutates allowance[_from][msg.sender] in transferFrom
msg.sender is the untrusted owner of the allowance written by approve(address _spender, uint _value)
msg.sender is used as the spender identity checked against allowance inside transferFrom
owner is directly derived from the untrusted msg.sender in the constructor
require(msg.sender == owner) is the only gate before the arbitrary delegatecall in delegate()
init() is guarded solely by require(msg.sender == owner) yet mutates global sale limits
batchSend() is owner-only but still performs unchecked arithmetic on user-supplied arrays
setTradeAddress() is owner-only and grants a whitelist bypass to an arbitrary account
The _from parameter drives the debit of balanceOf[_from] in transferFrom
The _to parameter is used to credit balanceOf[_to] in transferFrom
The _value parameter is subtracted from allowance and balance with raw -= instead of SafeMath
Attacker-influenced address a is the target of the delegatecall execution context switch
Raw bytes b is forwarded verbatim as calldata to the delegatecall target
delegate() unconditionally executes a.delegatecall(b), allowing arbitrary storage takeover
callOptionalReturn performs a low-level call on the supplied token contract
ABI-encoded calldata is passed into the low-level address(token).call(data)
_tos.length is multiplied by _value to compute total with no overflow guard
_value is reused as the per-recipient amount and balance debit inside batchSend
Local total = _value * _tos.length can silently overflow and under-debit the sender
The unchecked batchSend result is applied to balanceOf[msg.sender] and balanceOf[_to]
The loop index i controls how many unchecked balance credits execute in batchSend
Each _tos[i] recipient receives an unchecked balanceOf credit and Transfer event
transferFrom requires ensure(_from, _to, _value) which decides whether the transfer is authorized
ensure falls back to condition(_from, _value) when no whitelist entry matches
tradeAddress is compared against _from to grant an unconditional whitelist bypass in ensure
canSale[_from] allows a whitelisted account to skip the sell restriction checks
The owner address is whitelisted in ensure, bypassing all sale restrictions
condition() reads the _saleNum and related sale limit configuration when validating transfers
token is multiplied by 10**decimals inside init without overflow protection
maxToken is multiplied by 10**decimals inside init without overflow protection
The saleNum parameter is stored into the _saleNum state variable
Scaled token limits are written into the _minSale/_maxSale sale configuration
The addr parameter becomes the trusted tradeAddress used for whitelist bypasses
The spender parameter indexes the allowance mapping written by approve
The amount parameter is written as the new allowance value
approve directly stores _value into allowance[msg.sender][_spender] with no zero-allowance check
transfer forwards execution to transferFrom(msg.sender, _to, _value)
ensure() calls pairFor(...) to derive the Uniswap pair address checked against _from
The low-level external call to the token contract can re-enter balance-mutating functions such as transferFrom before state settles
delegatecall executes attacker code in this contract's storage context and can overwrite the owner slot, hijacking all privileged functions

normalization_plan.reason: _from is only meaningful as the debit identity of transferFrom
_to is only meaningful as the credit identity of transferFrom
_value is the operand of the unchecked allowance/balance subtraction
Target address a is the destination of the delegatecall in delegate()
Calldata b is executed verbatim by the delegatecall in delegate()
saleNum is a configuration argument consumed entirely by init()
token is the left operand of the unscaled multiplication in init()
maxToken is the left operand of the unscaled multiplication in init()
_tos.length is the multiplication factor driving the overflow in batchSend
_value is the per-recipient operand of the unchecked multiplication in batchSend
addr is the sole argument written to tradeAddress by the owner-only setter
data is the calldata payload supplied to the low-level token call
total exists only as the overflow-prone product inside batchSend
Loop index i exists only to drive the batchSend iteration
Local _to exists only as the loop recipient alias in batchSend
spender is the allowance key written by approve
amount is the allowance value written by approve
